target_claim: Let \(I=(\mathcal U,\mathcal C)\) be a \(k\)-set-packing instance with \(|\mathcal C|=n\), let \(\varepsilon>0\), and let \(M\subseteq\mathcal C\) be a \(4(1+1/\varepsilon)\log_2 n\)-locally optimal matching (that is, a packing of mutually disjoint sets). Let \(x\) be any feasible solution to the intersecting-family LP, let \(\mathcal F=\{f\in\mathcal C:x_f>0\}\), and let \(\mathcal F_2\) consist of those \(f\in\mathcal F\) that intersect exactly two members of \(M\). Define the auxiliary undirected multigraph \(H\) to have one vertex \(v_m\) for every \(m\in M\) and one edge \(e_f\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F_2\), joining \(v_{m_1}\) and \(v_{m_2}\) when \(m_1,m_2\) are the two members of \(M\) intersected by \(f\); distinct members of \(\mathcal F_2\) may therefore give parallel edges. For every \(X\subseteq V(H)\), let \(\mathcal B_X=\{f\in\mathcal F_2:e_f\in E(H[X])\}\). If \(|E(H[X])|>|X|\), then \(\mathcal B_X\) is an improving set for \(M\): \(\mathcal B_X\) is a packing and, in the intersection graph \(G\) of the packings \(M\) and \(\mathcal B_X\), \(N_G(B_X,M)=N(B_X)\cap M\) and \(\left|(M\cup B_X)\setminus N_G(B_X,M)\right|>|M|\). Equivalently, adding the source sets corresponding to the edges of \(H[X]\) and removing the members of \(M\) that they intersect yields a mutually disjoint solution of larger cardinality.
